# Ākaṅkheyya Sutta (MN 6 (PTS MN i 33))

**ID:** MN 6 (PTS MN i 33)
**Section:** Majjhimanikāya (mn)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-1
**Title (Pali):** Ākaṅkheyya Sutta
**PTS:** MN i 33
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0201m.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Ākaṅkheyya Sutta* (MN 6) is the sixth discourse of the *Majjhimanikāya*, set at Sāvatthi in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park [Ñāṇamoli & Bodhi 1995]. The discourse opens with the Buddha instructing monks to dwell accomplished in moral virtue, restrained by the disciplinary code (*pātimokkha-saṃvara-saṃvuta*), devoted to internal serenity, and dwelling in seclusion [Dutt 1924; Rogell 2003]. The Buddha presents ethical discipline and meditative cultivation as the indispensable foundation for fulfilling any spiritual desire or aspiration (*ākaṅkheyya*) [Rogell 2003]. These aspirations progress hierarchically from basic wishes—such as being loved and respected by fellow monastics or overcoming fear and anxiety in wilderness abodes—to mastering the four meditative absorptions (*jhāna*), acquiring supernormal powers and the six direct knowledges (*chalabhiññā*), and culminating in the destruction of the taints (*āsavakkhaya*) and awakening [Zhu 2017; Nyanaponika, Hecker & Bodhi 2003; Anālayo 2017; Melnikova 2014].

The sutta shares curated parallels with AN 10.71, AN 2.36, SN 47.46, and DN 2 (*Sāmaññaphala Sutta*) in the Pali canon, as well as MĀ 105 in the Chinese *Madhyamāgama* [Anālayo 2017]. A corresponding title (*agakṣaṇa*) is attested in a catalogue list of the Gāndhārī Senior Manuscripts [Allon 2014]. DharmaNexus confirms substantial Pali-internal text reuse (over 1,200 matches across 117 texts), showing near-total alignment between MN 6 §1.2–6.1 and AN 10.71, alongside shared doctrinal pericopes describing the supernormal knowledges with DN 2, MN 12, MN 77, and MN 108 [DharmaNexus; Zhu 2017]. Cross-linguistically, DharmaNexus matches parallel passages in the Chinese *Madhyamāgama* (T 26) and *Ekottarikāgama* (T 125), as well as formulaic descriptions preserved in Sanskrit and Tibetan versions of Mahāyāna texts such as the *Daśabalasūtra*, *Daśabhūmikasūtra*, and *Prajñāpāramitā* literature [DharmaNexus]. The sutta is also referenced in canonical and paracanonical works such as the *Vibhaṅga* and the *Milindapañha*.
